tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Colour Theory and Mixing

questions.question: Create a series of experimental studies exploring colour theory and mixing. Annotate your process.
questions.correctAnswer: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to colour theory and mixing, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes.

questions.question: Research an artist or designer who works with colour theory and mixing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work.
questions.correctAnswer: A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with colour theory and mixing. Which approaches were most successful and why?
questions.correctAnswer: A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Colour Theory and Mixing

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Select an artwork that uses colour expressively. Analyse the colour relationships and explain how the artist creates mood and meaning through colour. How has this informed your own colour choices? <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify specific colour schemes (complementary, analogous, triadic); analyse the emotional impact of colour choices; reference colour theory terminology; compare colour use across different artists; make thoughtful connections to personal work. Mark scheme: AO1 (develop through investigation) + AO2 (refine through experimentation) + AO3 (record ideas and observations) + AO4 (present personal response) = total marks
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
